resources.string: The emergency dialer could not be opened. Hold the power button and choose Emergency, if the power menu has it.
The call screen could not be opened. The call goes on until the other side hangs up, or until you switch the phone off from the power menu.
Quick power off waits until the call ends, so that it can never cut off an emergency call. To switch off now anyway, hold the power button and choose Power off.
The phone is in emergency callback mode, so that the emergency service can call back. Quick power off waits until that ends. To switch off now anyway, hold the power button and choose Power off.

resources.string: These choices last until you restart the phone. Until you start, the network stays closed.
Welcome is not the device owner, so it cannot apply Antumbra\'s protections. Set it up with adb first (see the README).
The Antumbra add-on is not running (its firewall has not reported in). Nothing else protects the network, so Wi-Fi will stay off for this session.
The usual choice. The network can see that you use Tor, but not what you do.
Hides from the network that you use Tor. Use it where Tor is blocked or watched.
No network for this session. Wi-Fi stays off.
The same bridges as in Tor Browser. They are blocked in some countries.
Not available yet: these obfs4 bridges need a part (lyrebird) that this version of Antumbra does not include.
From bridges.torproject.org, or from someone you trust.
Plain bridges (address:port and fingerprint). obfs4, webtunnel and meek_lite come later; Snowflake does not work here.
A random MAC address for this session, so networks cannot recognise the phone.
Networks can recognise this phone from earlier sessions.
Allows installing apps from outside the Antumbra store, Bluetooth, and turning Location on, until you restart the phone. USB debugging stays off. Off by default, as in Tails.
Coming later. For signing in to hotel or café Wi-Fi, without Tor.
Antumbra cannot start: Welcome is not the device owner, so none of its protections are in place. Set it up with adb first (see the README).
Antumbra cannot connect safely: some protections could not be applied (%1$s). Choose Stay offline, or restart the phone and try again.
A session from this start-up is still running in the add-on. Restart the phone to start a new one.
Enter at least one bridge line, or choose the built-in bridges.
Too many bridges: the limit is %1$d.
Line %1$d: Snowflake bridges do not work in Antumbra. Snowflake needs UDP, and the firewall lets Tor make only TCP connections. Use obfs4 or webtunnel bridges.
Line %1$d: unsupported bridge type “%2$s”. Antumbra takes obfs4, webtunnel, meek_lite and plain bridges.
Line %1$d: this line has a character that cannot be part of a bridge line.
Line %1$d is too long for a bridge line.
Line %1$d: IPv6 bridges do not work in Antumbra, because IPv6 is off. Use a bridge with an IPv4 address.
Line %1$d: “%2$s” is not an IPv4 address and port, such as 192.0.2.1:443.
Line %1$d: the fingerprint must be 40 hexadecimal characters.
Line %1$d: a %2$s bridge needs its %3$s part.
The built-in bridges are missing from this build of Welcome.
Line %1$d: %2$s bridges need a part (lyrebird) that this version of Antumbra does not include yet. Use plain bridges, or connect to Tor directly.
The session has not started yet.
A session is running, but Welcome no longer knows its choices.
Welcome was restarted after Start. The add-on keeps the choices made at Start until you restart the phone; to choose again, restart the phone.
Offline. Tor stays disconnected and Wi-Fi stays off until you restart.
Tor is not connecting: offline session.
The add-on has not reported Tor\'s progress yet.

The tracker filter is not answering.

Restarts the phone at once and ends this session. Memory can keep traces for a short while after a restart; when you have time, power off from the power menu instead.
